mq.DescribeBroker.doc: Returns information about the specified broker.

ActionRequiredCode.doc: The code you can use to find instructions on the action required to resolve your broker issue.

ActionRequiredInfo.doc: Information about the action required to resolve your broker issue.

AuthenticationStrategy.doc: The authentication strategy used to secure the broker. The default is SIMPLE.

AutoMinorVersionUpgrade.doc: Enables automatic upgrades to new patch versions for brokers as new versions are released and supported by Amazon MQ. Automatic upgrades occur during the scheduled maintenance window or after a manual broker reboot.

BrokerId.doc: The unique ID that Amazon MQ generates for the broker.

BrokerInstances.doc: A list of information about allocated brokers.

IpAddress.doc: The IP address of the Elastic Network Interface (ENI) attached to the broker. Does not apply to RabbitMQ brokers.

BrokerName.doc: The broker's name. This value must be unique in your Amazon Web Services account account, 1-50 characters long, must contain only letters, numbers, dashes, and underscores, and must not contain white spaces, brackets, wildcard characters, or special characters.

Configurations.doc: The list of all revisions for the specified configuration.

Id.doc: Required. The unique ID that Amazon MQ generates for the configuration.

Revision.doc: The revision number of the configuration.

History.doc: The history of configurations applied to the broker.

item.doc: A list of information about the configuration.

Id.doc: Required. The unique ID that Amazon MQ generates for the configuration.

Revision.doc: The revision number of the configuration.

Id.doc: Required. The unique ID that Amazon MQ generates for the configuration.

Revision.doc: The revision number of the configuration.

Created.doc: The time when the broker was created.

KmsKeyId.doc: The customer master key (CMK) to use for the A KMS (KMS). This key is used to encrypt your data at rest. If not provided, Amazon MQ will use a default CMK to encrypt your data.

UseAwsOwnedKey.doc: Enables the use of an Amazon Web Services owned CMK using KMS (KMS). Set to true by default, if no value is provided, for example, for RabbitMQ brokers.

EngineType.doc: The type of broker engine. Currently, Amazon MQ supports ACTIVEMQ and RABBITMQ.

EngineVersion.doc: The broker engine version. For more information, see the ActiveMQ version management and the RabbitMQ version management sections in the Amazon MQ Developer Guide.

LdapServerMetadata.doc: The metadata of the LDAP server used to authenticate and authorize connections to the broker.

Hosts.doc: Specifies the location of the LDAP server such as Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Optional failover server.

RoleBase.doc: The distinguished name of the node in the directory information tree (DIT) to search for roles or groups. For example, ou=group, ou=corp, dc=corp, dc=example, dc=com.

RoleName.doc: Specifies the LDAP attribute that identifies the group name attribute in the object returned from the group membership query.

RoleSearchMatching.doc: The LDAP search filter used to find roles within the roleBase. The distinguished name of the user matched by userSearchMatching is substituted into the {0} placeholder in the search filter. The client's username is substituted into the {1} placeholder. For example, if you set this option to (member=uid={1})for the user janedoe, the search filter becomes (member=uid=janedoe) after string substitution. It matches all role entries that have a member attribute equal to uid=janedoe under the subtree…

RoleSearchSubtree.doc: The directory search scope for the role. If set to true, scope is to search the entire subtree.

ServiceAccountUsername.doc: Service account username. A service account is an account in your LDAP server that has access to initiate a connection. For example, cn=admin,dc=corp, dc=example, dc=com.

UserBase.doc: Select a particular subtree of the directory information tree (DIT) to search for user entries. The subtree is specified by a DN, which specifies the base node of the subtree. For example, by setting this option to ou=Users,ou=corp, dc=corp, dc=example, dc=com, the search for user entries is restricted to the subtree beneath ou=Users, ou=corp, dc=corp, dc=example, dc=com.

UserRoleName.doc: Specifies the name of the LDAP attribute for the user group membership.

UserSearchMatching.doc: The LDAP search filter used to find users within the userBase. The client's username is substituted into the {0} placeholder in the search filter. For example, if this option is set to (uid={0}) and the received username is janedoe, the search filter becomes (uid=janedoe) after string substitution. It will result in matching an entry like uid=janedoe, ou=Users,ou=corp, dc=corp, dc=example, dc=com.

UserSearchSubtree.doc: The directory search scope for the user. If set to true, scope is to search the entire subtree.

Logs.doc: The list of information about logs currently enabled and pending to be deployed for the specified broker.

Audit.doc: Enables audit logging. Every user management action made using JMX or the ActiveMQ Web Console is logged.

AuditLogGroup.doc: The location of the CloudWatch Logs log group where audit logs are sent.

GeneralLogGroup.doc: The location of the CloudWatch Logs log group where general logs are sent.

Pending.doc: The list of information about logs pending to be deployed for the specified broker.

Audit.doc: Enables audit logging. Every user management action made using JMX or the ActiveMQ Web Console is logged.

MaintenanceWindowStartTime.doc: The parameters that determine the WeeklyStartTime.

DayOfWeek.doc: Required. The day of the week.

TimeZone.doc: The time zone, UTC by default, in either the Country/City format, or the UTC offset format.

PendingAuthenticationStrategy.doc: The authentication strategy that will be applied when the broker is rebooted. The default is SIMPLE.

PendingEngineVersion.doc: The broker engine version to upgrade to. For more information, see the ActiveMQ version management and the RabbitMQ version management sections in the Amazon MQ Developer Guide.

PendingHostInstanceType.doc: The broker's host instance type to upgrade to. For a list of supported instance types, see Broker instance types .

PendingLdapServerMetadata.doc: The metadata of the LDAP server that will be used to authenticate and authorize connections to the broker after it is rebooted.

Hosts.doc: Specifies the location of the LDAP server such as Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Optional failover server.

PendingSecurityGroups.doc: The list of pending security groups to authorize connections to brokers.

PubliclyAccessible.doc: Enables connections from applications outside of the VPC that hosts the broker's subnets.

SecurityGroups.doc: The list of rules (1 minimum, 125 maximum) that authorize connections to brokers.

SubnetIds.doc: The list of groups that define which subnets and IP ranges the broker can use from different Availability Zones.

Tags.doc: The list of all tags associated with this broker.

Users.doc: The list of all broker usernames for the specified broker.

item.doc: Returns a list of all broker users. Does not apply to RabbitMQ brokers.

PendingChange.doc: The type of change pending for the broker user.

Username.doc: Required. The username of the broker user. This value can contain only alphanumeric characters, dashes, periods, underscores, and tildes (- . _ ~). This value must be 2-100 characters long.

DataReplicationMetadata.doc: The replication details of the data replication-enabled broker. Only returned if dataReplicationMode is set to CRDR.

DataReplicationCounterpart.doc: Describes the replica/primary broker. Only returned if this broker is currently set as a primary or replica in the broker's dataReplicationRole property.

BrokerId.doc: Required. The unique broker id generated by Amazon MQ.

Region.doc: Required. The region of the broker.

DataReplicationRole.doc: Defines the role of this broker in a data replication pair. When a replica broker is promoted to primary, this role is interchanged.

DataReplicationMode.doc: Describes whether this broker is a part of a data replication pair.

PendingDataReplicationMetadata.doc: The pending replication details of the data replication-enabled broker. Only returned if pendingDataReplicationMode is set to CRDR.

DataReplicationCounterpart.doc: Describes the replica/primary broker. Only returned if this broker is currently set as a primary or replica in the broker's dataReplicationRole property.

BrokerId.doc: Required. The unique broker id generated by Amazon MQ.

Region.doc: Required. The region of the broker.

DataReplicationRole.doc: Defines the role of this broker in a data replication pair. When a replica broker is promoted to primary, this role is interchanged.

PendingDataReplicationMode.doc: Describes whether this broker will be a part of a data replication pair after reboot.

mq.ListBrokers.doc: Returns a list of all brokers.

BrokerSummaries.doc: A list of information about all brokers.

BrokerId.doc: The unique ID that Amazon MQ generates for the broker.

BrokerName.doc: The broker's name. This value is unique in your Amazon Web Services account, 1-50 characters long, and containing only letters, numbers, dashes, and underscores, and must not contain white spaces, brackets, wildcard characters, or special characters.

Created.doc: The time when the broker was created.

NextToken.doc: The token that specifies the next page of results Amazon MQ should return. To request the first page, leave nextToken empty.
